record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Does every oriented graph D have a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood has cardinality at least its out-neighborhood, that is, |N++(v)| >= |N+(v)|?

evidence.quote: Seymour’s Second Neighborhood Conjecture (SSNC) (see e.g., [29]) is one of the most interesting open problems on digraphs.
Conjecture 7.1 Every oriented graph D has a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood N ++(v) is not smaller than its out-neighborhood N +(v).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An oriented graph is a directed graph D=(V,E) with no loops and no pair of opposite arcs (i.e., for any two distinct vertices u,v at most one of (u,v),(v,u) is an arc). For a vertex v∈V, let N^+(v)={u∈V : (v,u)∈E} denote the first out-neighborhood of v, and let N^{++}(v) denote the second out-neighborhood of v, namely the set of vertices w∈V∖({v}∪N^+(v)) such that there exists u∈N^+(v) with (u,w)∈E.

Prove or disprove: every oriented graph D contains a vertex v such that
|N^{++}(v)| ≥ |N^+(v)|.
artifact.status_search_result: Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture remains open in its full generality as of 2025–2026. It has been verified for special classes (e.g., tournaments by Fisher, oriented graphs with minimum out-degree ≤ 6, and small orders). Recent work in 2024–2025 has improved the best constant c such that some vertex satisfies |N^{++}(v)| ≥ c·|N^+(v)| (now c ≈ 0.7155), and has established the conjecture for random orientations of G(n,p) for fixed p∈[0,1/2), but no general proof or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture: random graphs and reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Seymour's second neighbourhood conjecture states that in every oriented graph there is a vertex whose second outneighbourhood is at least as large as its outneighbourhood.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is stated as still open.

status_evidence.title: An improved bound on Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Proves existence of a vertex u with |N^{++}(u)| ≥ 0.715538|N^+(u)|, the first improvement in over two decades.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress; full conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Second neighborhood problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem in graph theory; proven only for special classes such as tournaments.
